subject.title: Hard-delete or runtimeId migration needed for @apify/apify-openclaw-plugin

question: Should an authorized ClawHub admin apply the runtimeId repair to the production Apify package, or choose a hard-delete/other migration path after verifying package ownership, collisions, and scan status?
rationale: This changes executable plugin identity and package reservation state in production, so source code cannot safely decide the data mutation without maintainer authority and security-boundary checks.

options.title: Run guarded runtimeId repair
options.body: Use the admin dry-run/apply flow after verifying Apify ownership, current package state, suspicious scan status, and no active runtimeId collision.

options.title: Hard-delete or retire entry
options.body: Use a destructive package repair path only if the runtimeId repair cannot preserve the intended package identity safely.

options.title: Wait for stronger identity proof
options.body: Keep the package blocked until maintainers have enough publisher-admin verification to mutate the production record.

recommendation.title: Run guarded runtimeId repair
recommendation.body: Use the admin dry-run/apply flow after verifying Apify ownership, current package state, suspicious scan status, and no active runtimeId collision.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the package identity/runtimeId admin repair flows and handled the analogous OpenViking repair.
